message_id.format: A three- to six-digit integer, the id in %ASA-<level>-<id>.

111008.meaning: The user entered any command except a show command.

111009.meaning: The user entered a command that does not modify the configuration; this message appears only for show commands.

111010.meaning: A user made a configuration change; carries the username, the application it ran from, the source IP and the command.

113006.meaning: A locally configured user was locked out after exceeding the configured number of consecutive failed authentication attempts.

302013.meaning: A TCP connection slot between two hosts was created.

302014.meaning: A TCP connection between two hosts was deleted; carries duration, bytes and the termination reason.
302014.note: observed: TCP Reset-O from identity, duration 0:00:00, bytes 1585

502101.meaning: A new username record was added to the local database, with username, privilege level and a masked password.

502102.meaning: A username record was deleted from the local database, with username, privilege level and a masked password.

502103.meaning: A local user's privilege level was changed from one level to another.

609001.meaning: A network state container was reserved for a host connected to a zone.
609001.note: not exemplified in this pack's sample; 609002 (its teardown pair) was

609002.meaning: A network state container for a host connected to a zone was removed; carries the zone, the host address and a duration.

710005.meaning: A TCP, UDP or SCTP request was discarded because ASA has no server or session for it; high-volume broadcast traffic (DHCP, RIP, NetBIOS) is a common cause, not only an attack.
710005.note: observed: TCP request discarded from 198.27.166.158/55607 to management:172.31.12.229/443

examples.note: most frequent id in the sampled attack_data (50 of ~330 events)

severity_level.format: One fixed word, the RFC 5424 name of the syslog level.

level_description.format: One fixed sentence, matched one-to-one with log_level. Reads like a summary of the event; it is actually the syslog level's own fixed gloss, identical on every record at that level.

action.format: One lower-case word, from a lookup keyed on the raw action token or on message_id. cisco_asa_action_lookup_600.csv carries well over a hundred rows; only the values this pack's sample or the CIM-prescribed set exercised are listed.

read.meaning: A non-modifying (show) command was read; the message_id-keyed action for 111009.

executed.meaning: A vendor_action-keyed row for a raw "executed" token; not the action seen on 111008 or 111010 in this pack's sample, which resolve via message_id to read/modified instead.

modified.meaning: A configuration was changed; the message_id-keyed action for 111010.

created.meaning: An account or object was created; the message_id-keyed action for 502101.

deleted.meaning: An account or object was deleted; the message_id-keyed action for 502102 and the vendor_action-keyed row for a raw "deleted" token.

vendor_action.format: One lower-case word, Cisco's own verb before CIM normalization, or a literal (blocked, flow) for two message-id groups this pack's sample did not exercise.

built.meaning: A connection slot was created; normalizes to action=allowed.

teardown.meaning: A connection was torn down; normalizes to action=teardown.

discarded.meaning: A request was discarded; normalizes to action=blocked.

blocked.meaning: EVAL literal for message ids 313005 and 338002; not exemplified in this pack's sample.

flow.meaning: EVAL literal for message ids 400013, 419002, 419003 and 500003; not exemplified in this pack's sample.

severity.format: One lower-case word: a literal for six message ids, else from the signature_id lookup that also sets vendor_severity. None of this pack's sampled message ids (111008-113006, 302013/302014, 502101-502103, 609002, 710005) hit either path, so no value is exemplified.

informational.meaning: EVAL literal for message ids 106016, 106017, 400032 and 110003.

status.format: The literal success for a fixed list of message ids (including every id this pack sampled that carries a status at all), else whatever status the extraction set.

success.meaning: EVAL literal; observed on 111009, 111010, 502101, 502102 and 502103 in this pack's sample.

category.format: A literal for three message-id groups, else the extracted category. Not exemplified in this pack's sample; read from the live EVAL.

DOS.meaning: EVAL literal for message ids 400032 and 106017.

app.format: A literal for six message-id groups, else the extracted app. Not exemplified in this pack's sample; read from the live EVAL.

ASA.meaning: EVAL literal for message ids 106012, 302016, 611101, 713166 and 713167.

Firewall.meaning: EVAL literal for message ids 110003 and 405001.

object_category.format: A literal for four message ids, else the extracted object_category, lower-cased.

user.meaning: The REGEX-captured value on the 502101/502102/502103 messages this pack sampled (User priv level changed:/User deleted from local dbase:/New user added to local dbase: all start with the word User); not the same as the EVAL's own literal set.

object.format: A per-message-id literal (src, command, user, "user account", process_name) for six message ids, else coalesce(object, object_id).

examples.note: 111010, equals process_name, which the sampled line left unset

object_path.format: One fixed word in the samples this pack read.

local.meaning: The on-box local user database, on the 502101/502102 messages.

icmp.meaning: Internet Control Message Protocol; forces every *_port field on the record to 0.

protocol.format: One fixed word; on this sourcetype only two values are reachable.

ip.meaning: transport is tcp or udp (or message id 338301). Not the transport name itself.

inbound.meaning: The original connection was initiated from outside the interface.

outbound.meaning: The original connection was initiated from inside the interface; also set when the raw value was egress.

ids_type.format: One fixed word; a literal on every record of this sourcetype.

network.meaning: The only value cisco:asa ever sets; CIM also allows host, application and wireless for other products.

ssl_is_valid.format: failed and validated are normalized to false/true; other raw values pass through unchanged.

type.format: A literal for three message ids, else whatever type the extraction already set. Not exemplified in this pack's sample.

result.format: Free text: the command itself for message id 111009, else the extraction's lead phrase.

examples.value: New user added to local dbase

privilege_level.format: An integer, 0 to 15, the ASA exec privilege scale.

encrypted_password.format: A fixed masked string in every sample seen; never the real credential.

examples.note: 502101, 502102; ASA itself writes this literal, not this pack

process_name.format: Free text, an application name, or N/A when the CLI session names none.

parent_process_name.format: The quoted command text at the end of a 111010 message.

dest_port.format: An integer 0 to 65535; forced to 0 for icmp. Four sibling fields split one NATed flow's destination port three ways (dest_port, dest_public_port, dest_translated_port); src_port/src_public_port/src_translated_port mirror this on the source side. Their own entries are left thin to keep this sidecar under budget; the same icmp-forces-0 rule applies to all six.

examples.note: 302013, 302014, 710005, coalesced in from service on the last

dvc.format: The reporting host's address, aliased from Splunk's own host field.

examples.note: every record in this pack's sample

object_attrs.format: A literal list for three message-id groups, else the extracted value lower-cased.
